page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Left margin: one marginal note beside the paragraph's middle section. Top: page number and running head. Bottom right: catchword.
page.running_head: De Agro Frisi inter Lavic. & Amas.

main_text.p: collegiis aut nunquam, aut omninò rarissimè quisquam caperetur. Indignum enim id concilio honoratissimo, & Reip. periculosum propter abjectos hujusmodi hominum sensus praeter lucrum penè nihil spectantes, aut magni facientes putabatur. Hoc verò praetereundum hic silentio non est, non semul accidisse olim rebus sic poscentibus, aut factionum vi, ut exposita ratio in designandis quotannis Consulibus duobus dimidiaque senatûs parte observata non fit; sed consules iidem omnes vel biennium, vel ad annos complures, vel denique ad vitae exitum in munere ac honore permanserint: i-De Oldermanno, & tribunali jus [?]demque sit factum in reliquo senatu. Est praeterea aliud in civitate collegium, partem Reip. curans, negotiantium scilicet disciplinae, ac juri nautico tuendo, & dirimendis indè natis controversiis olim praesectum, cujus tribunal Gilderecht [?] lingua Teutonica ex re nominatum. O-cto viris constat hodiè; quorum etiam, ut senatorum, & eorum qui sunt in concilio jurato, munus est bienne, quaternis similiter quotannis collegio decedenti-[?]
{ } Catchword "tibus" read from the foot of the page at the right; taken as the next word.

page.notes: The left margin note is printed in three lines, "De Ol- / dermanno, & tri- / bunaliejus", with the hyphenated word joined here; the final word "bunaliejus" is doubtful and read as "tribunali jus". The word after "tribunal" is in black letter and is read as "Gilderecht" with [?]. The last line ends with a hyphen and the catchword "tibus" does not clearly complete it, so the reading "decedenti-" is doubtful. The running head is read with long s as "Frisi" and "Amas", the printed f-forms being long s; "Lavic." is as printed. The "O" of "Octo" is read as the printed "Oëto" and transcribed as "Octo". No printing errors are certain.
